senses.gloss: A course of action someone turns to when nothing else has worked.
examples: Surgery is a last *resort*, not a first step.
They settled the dispute without *resort* to the courts.
Calling his parents was a desperate last *resort*.

senses.gloss: A silence of a set length in written music.
examples: Hold the *rest* for two full beats before you come in.
The piece opens with a quarter *rest*.
She counted the *rests* under her breath.

senses.gloss: Something that happens because of an earlier action or event.
examples: The flooding was a direct *result* of the storm.
Prices went up as a *result* of the new tariff.
Skipping practice had *results* he didn't like.

senses.gloss: The act of coming back to a place or to an earlier condition.
examples: We celebrated his *return* from Afghanistan.
Her *return* to work is set for Monday.
The team's *return* to the playoffs took nine years.

senses.gloss: An item taken back to the store where it was bought.
examples: The customer service desk handles all *returns*.
This shirt is a *return*, so it's marked down.
There are no *returns* on final-sale items.

senses.gloss: The form you file every year reporting your income to the government.
examples: I still haven't filed my tax *return*.
Her accountant found an error on last year's *return*.
You can e-file a simple *return* in twenty minutes.

senses.gloss: The opposite of what has just been said or expected.
examples: I thought he'd be angry, but the *reverse* was true.
The order of names is the *reverse* of last year's.
Far from helping, it did the *reverse*.

senses.gloss: The back side of a coin, medal, or sheet of paper.
examples: The *reverse* of the quarter shows an eagle.
Sign your name on the *reverse* of the check.
The date is stamped on the *reverse*.

senses.gloss: A written opinion of a movie, book, restaurant, or product.
examples: The movie got terrible *reviews*.
I read a *review* of the new Thai place downtown.
The hotel has four stars and hundreds of *reviews*.

senses.gloss: A return of interest in something, or a return to strength after a decline.
examples: The neighborhood is enjoying a real *revival*.
There's been a *revival* of interest in vinyl records.
Cheap gas fueled a *revival* of big trucks.

senses.gloss: A series of religious meetings held to reawaken people's faith.
examples: A tent *revival* came through town every August.
Her grandfather preached at *revivals* across the South.
The church is holding a week-long *revival*.

senses.gloss: A regular pattern in which events or movements repeat over time.
examples: Farm work follows the *rhythm* of the seasons.
Night shifts threw off his body's natural *rhythm*.
I finally settled into the *rhythm* of the new job.

senses.gloss: A machine at a fair or amusement park that people get on for fun.
examples: The kids went straight for the *rides*.
That *ride* spins you upside down twice.
You have to be four feet tall for this *ride*.

senses.gloss: A person's car, in informal speech.
examples: Nice *ride* — is it new?
He washes his *ride* every Sunday.
My *ride* is in the shop until Thursday.

senses.gloss: A long raised line along the surface of something.
examples: Snow slid off both sides of the roof *ridge*.
You can feel the *ridges* on a corduroy jacket.
The chip has *ridges* so it won't break in the dip.

senses.gloss: A short stretch of talk that plays with one idea, often for laughs.
examples: He did a five-minute *riff* on airport security.
Her column is a *riff* on modern parenting.
The show opens with a *riff* about the weather.

senses.gloss: The side or direction opposite the left.
examples: Take a *right* at the second light.
The bakery is on your *right*.
He looked to the *right* before pulling out.

senses.gloss: The conservative side in politics.
examples: The bill drew fire from the *right*.
She's well to the *right* of her own party.
Voters on the *right* stayed home.

senses.gloss: A circle, or a circular mark or arrangement of things.
examples: The mug left a *ring* on the table.
The children sat in a *ring* around the teacher.
You can count the *rings* to tell the tree's age.

senses.gloss: The square platform where boxers or wrestlers fight.
examples: The champ climbed into the *ring* to a huge cheer.
He was knocked out of the *ring* in the third round.
The elephants entered the center *ring*.

senses.gloss: An organized group of people working together at something illegal.
examples: Police broke up a car-theft *ring*.
A smuggling *ring* operated out of the port for years.
Two officers were tied to the drug *ring*.

senses.gloss: The sound made by a bell or a phone.
examples: The *ring* of the doorbell woke everyone up.
She picked up on the first *ring*.
I heard the *ring* of church bells across the valley.

senses.gloss: Someone or something extremely funny, in informal speech.
examples: Your uncle is a *riot* at parties.
That movie was a *riot* from start to finish.
The bloopers at the end are a total *riot*.

senses.gloss: A feeling, sound, or effect that spreads gradually through a group.
examples: A *ripple* of laughter ran through the audience.
The layoffs sent *ripples* through the whole town.
There was a *ripple* of applause when she finished.

senses.gloss: A place where the ground slopes upward.
examples: The house sits on a small *rise* above the river.
You'll see the barn once you're over the *rise*.
We pulled the sled up the *rise* and rode back down.

senses.gloss: The chance that something bad will happen.
examples: Smoking raises your *risk* of heart disease.
There's no *risk* of frost this late in the spring.
He took a *risk* and quit without another job lined up.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that could cause harm or loss.
examples: That pile of oily rags is a fire *risk*.
The bank considered him a poor credit *risk*.
The loose railing is a safety *risk*.

senses.gloss: Loud popular music played mainly on guitars and drums.
examples: He grew up on classic *rock*.
The station plays *rock* all afternoon.
Her first band was straight-ahead *rock*.

senses.gloss: Someone who stays steady and supports you through hard times.
examples: My sister was my *rock* that whole year.
He's been a *rock* for the family since the accident.
Every team needs a *rock* in the locker room.

senses.gloss: A character played by an actor in a movie, play, or show.
examples: She won an award for her *role* in the film.
He auditioned for the lead *role*.
The director cast unknowns in the smaller *roles*.

senses.gloss: A small tube that hair is wound onto to make it curl.
examples: She answered the door with *rollers* still in her hair.
Heat the *rollers* for ten minutes first.
My grandmother slept in *rollers* every night.

senses.gloss: A turning cylinder inside a machine that moves or presses things.
examples: A worn *roller* was jamming the printer.
Boxes slid down the conveyor on metal *rollers*.
The shop replaced the *rollers* in the garage door.

senses.gloss: Anyone who is new and inexperienced at a job or activity.
examples: He's a *rookie* cop, three weeks out of the academy.
That was a *rookie* mistake and she knew it.
The *rookies* got all the night shifts.

senses.gloss: The basic cause or source of a problem or situation.
examples: Money is at the *root* of most of their arguments.
We need to get to the *root* of the problem.
The report traced the *roots* of the crisis to 2008.

senses.gloss: The family, place, or culture a person comes from.
examples: Her *roots* are in a small town in Kansas.
He went to Ireland to look into his *roots*.
The festival celebrates the city's Mexican *roots*.

senses.gloss: The part of a tooth or a hair that sits below the surface.
examples: The dentist said the *root* was infected.
Her dark *roots* were starting to show.
The shampoo adds volume at the *roots*.

senses.gloss: One stage in a competition or in a series of events.
examples: They were knocked out in the first *round*.
I made it to the final *round* of interviews.
The next *round* of talks starts in April.

senses.gloss: A single bullet or shell for a gun.
examples: He fired three *rounds* into the target.
The magazine holds fifteen *rounds*.
There was one *round* left in the chamber.

senses.gloss: A regular series of visits made as part of a job.
examples: The doctor is on her morning *rounds*.
The mail carrier finishes his *round* by two.
Security makes *rounds* of the building every hour.

senses.gloss: A numbered highway.
examples: Take *Route* 9 north for about ten miles.
The diner sits right off the old *route*.
Both *routes* run parallel to the river.

senses.gloss: The fixed set of stops a person covers to deliver something.
examples: He had a paper *route* when he was twelve.
Her delivery *route* covers three neighborhoods.
The driver's *route* changed after the merger.

senses.gloss: A box that connects the devices in a home or office to the internet.
examples: Try unplugging the *router* and plugging it back in.
The Wi-Fi *router* sits in the hall closet.
Our old *router* couldn't handle four laptops.

senses.gloss: A set piece performed by a dancer, gymnast, or comedian.
examples: She nailed her floor *routine*.
The comedian opened with his airport *routine*.
They practiced the dance *routine* for weeks.

senses.gloss: A line of boxes running across a table or spreadsheet.
examples: Put the totals in the bottom *row*.
Each *row* holds one customer's information.
Delete the empty *rows* before you print it.

senses.gloss: Kings, queens, and the members of their families.
examples: The crowd hoped to catch a glimpse of *royalty*.
They were treated like *royalty* all weekend.
The museum displays jewelry once worn by *royalty*.

senses.gloss: A mix of dry spices pressed onto meat before it is cooked.
examples: He puts a brown-sugar *rub* on the ribs.
The *rub* is mostly paprika, salt, and pepper.
Let the *rub* sit on the brisket overnight.

senses.gloss: The power to govern a country or people, or the period of that power.
examples: The island was under Spanish *rule* for centuries.
The country returned to civilian *rule* in 1990.
Life under military *rule* was tightly controlled.

senses.gloss: A person who governs a country or people.
examples: He was the last *ruler* of the old kingdom.
The *ruler* refused to give up power.
Ancient *rulers* were buried with their treasure.

senses.gloss: A period of running for exercise.
examples: I go for a *run* before work most days.
That was a slow five-mile *run*.
Her morning *runs* keep her sane.

senses.gloss: A point scored in baseball when a player reaches home plate.
examples: They scored four *runs* in the seventh inning.
One more *run* would have tied the game.
He drove in the winning *run*.

senses.gloss: A stretch of time in which the same kind of thing keeps happening.
examples: The team is on a six-game winning *run*.
She's had a bad *run* of luck this year.
After a long *run* of warm days, it finally rained.

senses.gloss: A line where the threads have come apart in a stocking.
examples: There's a *run* in my pantyhose.
Clear nail polish will stop the *run* from spreading.
She noticed the *run* right before the interview.

senses.gloss: A long narrow strip of cloth or carpet laid on a table, hall, or stairs.
examples: A linen *runner* went down the middle of the table.
They put a *runner* on the stairs so nobody slips.
The hallway *runner* needs cleaning.

senses.gloss: One of the long narrow blades a sled or a skate slides on.
examples: The sled's *runners* were caked with ice.
He waxed the *runners* to make it go faster.
One *runner* had bent in the crash.

senses.gloss: A stem a plant sends out along the ground to start new plants.
examples: Strawberries spread by sending out *runners*.
Snip the *runners* if you want bigger berries.
The plant put out a *runner* into the next bed.

senses.gloss: Rain or melted snow that flows off the land into streams and rivers.
examples: Fertilizer in the *runoff* is polluting the lake.
Spring *runoff* swelled the creek past its banks.
The ditch carries *runoff* away from the road.

senses.gloss: A sudden strong feeling or burst of energy.
examples: He felt a *rush* of adrenaline as the doors opened.
Skydiving gave her a *rush* she never forgot.
There was a *rush* of relief when the results came back.

senses.gloss: A deep track worn into soft ground by wheels.
examples: The truck sank into a muddy *rut*.
Frozen *ruts* made the dirt road rough.
Rain had cut deep *ruts* across the driveway.

senses.gloss: A dull routine that a person cannot seem to break out of.
examples: I'm in a *rut* at work and need a change.
They fell into a *rut* of takeout and TV.
A trip might shake her out of this *rut*.

senses.gloss: A whiskey distilled mostly from rye grain.
examples: He ordered a *rye* on the rocks.
The bar keeps three kinds of *rye*.
This cocktail works better with *rye* than bourbon.

senses.gloss: A play in football in which the quarterback is tackled behind the line.
examples: He had three *sacks* in the first half.
The *sack* pushed them back fifteen yards.
Their defense leads the league in *sacks*.

senses.gloss: The catch on a gun that keeps it from firing.
examples: Keep the *safety* on until you're ready to shoot.
He forgot to flip the *safety* off.
The rifle has a *safety* right above the trigger.

senses.gloss: A very wise person, especially an older one.
examples: The old man was treated as the village *sage*.
Reporters quoted him like some kind of *sage*.
Ancient *sages* wrote about the same questions.

senses.gloss: A trip taken in a sailboat.
examples: We went for a *sail* around the harbor.
It was a rough *sail* back to the dock.
A sunset *sail* costs forty dollars a person.

senses.gloss: A very kind or endlessly patient person.
examples: You'd have to be a *saint* to put up with that.
His wife is a *saint* for driving him every week.
The nurses on that floor are *saints*.

senses.gloss: A lively Latin American dance, or the music played for it.
examples: They take *salsa* lessons on Thursday nights.
The band played *salsa* until two in the morning.
She learned to dance *salsa* in Miami.

senses.gloss: A small free portion given out so people can try a product.
examples: They were handing out *samples* of the new cereal.
The counter gave me a *sample* of the perfume.
Free *samples* always draw a crowd.

senses.gloss: A short piece of an existing recording used in a new song.
examples: The chorus is built around a *sample* from a 70s record.
He cleared the *sample* before releasing the track.
You can hear two *samples* layered under the beat.

senses.gloss: A separated area where new software can be tested safely.
examples: Run the code in a *sandbox* first.
The bank gives developers a *sandbox* to test payments.
Nothing in the *sandbox* touches real customer data.

senses.gloss: A foolish person who is easy to fool, in informal speech.
examples: Some poor *sap* paid full price for it.
Don't be a *sap* and lend him money again.
He felt like a *sap* for believing the story.
